# Curated conformance matrix, shared by ci.yml and nightly.yml.
#
# One resource fixture per line. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are
# ignored, so an excluded fixture stays here commented with the reason it is out
# and the local command that still exercises it.
#
# This file is the single source of truth for BOTH workflows: ci.yml gates every
# push and PR on it, nightly.yml runs the same list against formae main. It exists
# because the two matrices were maintained by hand and drifted - nightly was still
# running 30 of the 130 entries CI ran, so 100 resources had no nightly coverage
# at all. Editing this file changes both.
#
# The matrix is curated rather than auto-discovered from testdata/: a fixture only
# belongs here once it passes CRUD *and* discovery against live Azure.
#
# To run ONE fixture (or a few) instead of the whole matrix, dispatch CI by hand:
#
#   gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f resources=redis-cache
#   gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f resources='redis-cache, event-hub' -f phase=crud
#
# or use the "Run workflow" button on the CI workflow in the Actions tab. Any
# fixture with a testdata/<name>.pkl may be named, including ones commented out
# below - that is how you re-check an exclusion without editing this file. An
# unknown name fails the run rather than quietly testing nothing. phase is
# both (default), crud or discovery.

resource-group
virtual-network
subnet
network-security-group
public-ip-address
storage-account
registry
vault
# flexible-server and firewall-rule excluded due to formae core
# discovery persistence bug (discovered resources not appearing in inventory).
# CRUD tests still run via test-integration.
role-assignment
user-assigned-identity
federated-identity-credential
load-balancer
application-gateway
waf-policy
# certificate (AZURE::KeyVault::Certificate) excluded: like `secret`, it is a
# Key Vault DATA-PLANE resource — the CI principal can create the vault via ARM
# but cannot write certificates without the "Key Vault Certificates Officer"
# role. CRUD is validated via test-integration (mocked); run live locally with:
# make conformance-test-crud TEST=certificate
dns-zone
dns-record-set
private-dns-zone
private-dns-vnet-link
private-endpoint
private-dns-zone-group
blob-container
disk
virtual-machine-scale-set
# Azure Front Door Standard (Microsoft.Cdn AFD). Profile provisioning is
# minutes-slow + billed; each fixture stands up the chain up to its own
# resource (cdn-route brings up the full profile→endpoint→origin-group→
# origin→route AFD). Uses TIMEOUT overrides in the run step.
cdn-profile
cdn-afd-endpoint
cdn-afd-origin-group
cdn-afd-origin
# cdn-route excluded: the Route references TWO sibling resources created in
# the same apply (origin group + endpoint), which reliably trips the formae
# core resolve-cache race (ResolveCacheMissingInAction) on first apply — the
# route aborts in the "resolving" state while its siblings succeed around it
# (3/3 live attempts). NOT a plugin bug: Route marshalling is covered by
# TestCdnRoute_MarshallerRoundTrip and profile/endpoint/origin-group/origin all
# pass live. Re-enable once the core resolve-cache race is fixed. Run locally:
# make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-route
# cdn-afd-custom-domain and cdn-secret excluded: custom-domain needs a REAL
# owned domain (Azure _dnsauth TXT ownership challenge) and secret needs a
# real Key Vault certificate + AFD service-principal vault access — neither
# is available to the CI principal. CRUD validated via test-integration
# (mocked) + marshaller round-trip; run live locally with a real domain/cert:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-afd-custom-domain
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-secret
# --- Private DNS resolver family. All free (the resolver and its endpoints
# bill nothing; only the vnet and subnet exist alongside) and each
# provisions in ~2-4 min.
dns-resolver
dns-resolver-inbound-endpoint
dns-resolver-outbound-endpoint
dns-forwarding-ruleset
dns-forwarding-rule
dns-forwarding-ruleset-vnet-link
# --- DNS security policy. Also free.
dns-resolver-policy
dns-resolver-policy-vnet-link
dns-resolver-domain-list
dns-security-rule
# --- Azure Firewall policy. The policy and its rule collection groups are
# free without an attached firewall, and none is created.
firewall-policy
firewall-policy-rule-collection-group
# --- Remaining networking. subnet-delegated covers subnet delegation on its
# own, independent of the resolver endpoints that consume it.
subnet-delegated
vnet-peering
traffic-manager-profile
# local-network-gateway excluded from the matrix: armnetwork offers no
# subscription-wide listing for the type (only NewListPager(resourceGroup)),
# and the gateway has no parent resource for discovery to hand a group down
# from — so the discovery phase can never see it, though CRUD passes. CRUD is
# validated via test-integration (mocked); run live locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=local-network-gateway
# --- Azure Monitor alerting. Action groups and activity log alerts are free;
# a metric alert and a scheduled query rule are ~$0.10-0.15/month each and
# are deleted by the run.
action-group
activity-log-alert
metric-alert
scheduled-query-rule
# --- Azure Monitor Agent ingestion. Both free; nothing is collected because
# no machine is associated with the rule.
data-collection-endpoint
data-collection-rule
# --- Azure Monitor private link. Free: the scope and its scoped resources
# carry no charge, and the private endpoint that would bill is not created.
private-link-scope
private-link-scoped-resource
# --- Log Analytics and Application Insights. The workspace is PerGB2018 with
# a 1 GB daily cap and nothing sends data to it; destroy soft-deletes it for
# 14 days, so fixtures carry the run ID in the name.
log-analytics-workspace
app-insights-component
saved-search
data-export
linked-storage-account
# diagnostic-setting excluded from the matrix: a diagnostic setting hangs off
# an arbitrary target resource, addressed by that resource's URI, so listing
# them means enumerating every resource in the subscription first. Discovery
# has no parent to supply the URI and the phase times out. CRUD passes; run
# live locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=diagnostic-setting
# --- Governance. Custom roles and policy are free, and the conformance
# fixtures stay harmless on a shared subscription: the policy effect is
# `audit` and the assignment pins enforcementMode DoNotEnforce, scoped to the
# test resource group rather than the subscription.
role-definition
policy-definition
policy-set-definition
policy-assignment
# --- Relay. A namespace is ~$0.10/month prorated; hybrid connections and
# authorization rules are free. No listen/send keys are read into state.
relay-namespace
relay-hybrid-connection
# relay-namespace-auth-rule and relay-hc-auth-rule excluded: the plugin does
# return them ("Received 1 resources for AZURE::Relay::NamespaceAuthorizationRule"
# in the job log) but they never reach the inventory — the same formae-core
# discovery persistence bug that already excludes flexible-server and
# firewall-rule above. CRUD passes for both.
# --- Notification Hubs. Free tier namespace; PNS credentials are inputs the
# provider never sends back, so an out-of-band credential survives an apply.
notification-hub-namespace
notification-hub
nh-auth-rule
# --- Messaging odds and ends. Service Bus needs a Standard namespace for
# topics/subscriptions (~$10/month prorated to the run); the Event Hubs schema
# group and Event Grid subscription are free.
service-bus-rule
# service-bus-authorization-rule excluded for the same core persistence bug as
# the relay authorization rules above: listed by the plugin, absent from
# inventory.
schema-group
# event-grid-event-subscription excluded from the matrix: an event
# subscription is a scoped extension resource whose scope is any ARM ID — a
# topic, a storage account, the subscription itself — and the schema carries
# that scope as one opaque string rather than as resource group + provider +
# type + name. ARM's per-resource listing needs those four parts, so discovery
# has nothing to hand down, and the subscription-wide listing the provider
# falls back to returns only subscription-LEVEL subscriptions, not the
# topic-scoped one the fixture creates. CRUD passes; run live locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=event-grid-event-subscription
# --- Remaining resources, added wholesale so one CI run shows which of them
# the discovery phase can actually see. Discovery needs either a
# subscription-wide List or a parent chain to hand scope down; a resource
# with neither is invisible to it however well its CRUD lifecycle works.
# Expected to pass both phases (each has a subscription-wide List):
app-configuration-store
batch-account
container-group
cosmos-database-account
disk-access
iot-hub
# mysql-flexible-server excluded: discovery works but formae-core never persists the
# result. The plugin's List returns the resource ("Received 1 resources
# for AZURE::DBforMySQL::FlexibleServer") yet the discovery gate still fails with "resource did not
# appear in inventory". Same core bug flexible-server/firewall-rule
# already carry. CRUD passes and still runs locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=mysql-flexible-server
# - mysql-flexible-server
netapp-account
redis-cache
search-service
signalr-service
web-pubsub
# Parent-scoped, so discovery depends on the parent chain resolving:

# result. The plugin's List returns the resource ("Received 1 resources
# for AZURE::ContainerRegistry::Webhook") yet the discovery gate still fails with "resource did not
# appear in inventory". Same core bug flexible-server/firewall-rule
# already carry. CRUD passes and still runs locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=acr-webhook
# - acr-webhook
scope-map
registry-token
# gallery-application excluded: discovery works but formae-core never persists the
# result. The plugin's List returns the resource ("Received 1 resources
# for AZURE::Compute::GalleryApplication") yet the discovery gate still fails with "resource did not
# appear in inventory". Same core bug flexible-server/firewall-rule
# already carry. CRUD passes and still runs locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=gallery-application
# - gallery-application
sql-elastic-pool

# Unclear: lists per resource group with no subscription-wide fallback.
backup-vault
# --- Fixtures that existed without ever being gated. Every resource in the
# plugin ships a conformance fixture, but the matrix is hand-maintained, so
# 45 of them had never run in CI or nightly — including three types merged
# last week (compute-gallery, compute-gallery-image, compute-snapshot). They
# are listed here so a regression in any of them fails a PR rather than
# going unnoticed.
#
# Networking and identity primitives. All free and fast.
application-security-group
ip-group
nat-gateway
public-ip-prefix
route-table
private-dns-record-set
network-watcher
# network-watcher-flow-log excluded: a flow log is created inside Azure's
# own auto-provisioned NetworkWatcherRG resource group, not the test's
# resource group, so the discovery gate never sees it - AZURE::Network::FlowLog
# is not enumerated at all in the run. Not a plugin bug: the List has both a
# per-watcher path and a subscription-wide NewListAllWatchersPager fallback.
# CRUD passes and still runs locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=network-watcher-flow-log
# - network-watcher-flow-log
ssh-public-key
proximity-placement-group
# availability-set excluded: discovery works but formae-core never persists the
# result. The plugin's List returns the resource ("Received 1 resources
# for AZURE::Compute::AvailabilitySet") yet the discovery gate still fails with "resource did not
# appear in inventory". Same core bug flexible-server/firewall-rule
# already carry. CRUD passes and still runs locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=availability-set
# - availability-set

# SQL. The server itself is free; the fixtures that create a database use the
# cheapest tier. Server provisioning is a few minutes, hence the timeout
# override below.
sql-server
sql-database
sql-firewall-rule
sql-outbound-firewall-rule
sql-virtual-network-rule
sql-server-dns-alias
# sql-ad-administrator excluded: Create fails outright because the fixture
# carries a placeholder sid/tenantId and Azure requires a real Azure AD
# principal. Nightly excludes it for the same reason. CRUD is validated via
# test-integration (mocked); run live locally against a real principal:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=sql-ad-administrator
# - sql-ad-administrator
# Other services. cognitive-services-account uses the free F0 tier;
# configuration and database are children of stores created by their own
# fixtures.
# cognitive-services-account excluded: Replace reaches a terminal Failed
# state. The kind under test needs subscription quota/approval the CI
# principal does not hold. Nightly excludes it for the same reason.
# CRUD is validated via test-integration (mocked); run live locally on an
# approved subscription:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cognitive-services-account
# - cognitive-services-account
# configuration excluded: with the per-command poll raised to 20 min the whole
# CRUD lifecycle now gets as far as Destroy, which then reaches a terminal Failed
# state in about one second - not a timeout. AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::Configuration
# is a server setting rather than a deletable child, so the plugin implements
# Delete as "reset to the default value via BeginUpdate"; that update is what
# Azure rejects. The core does not surface the Azure error text, so the message
# still has to be read off a local run:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=configuration
# configuration
# database excluded: CRUD passes end to end (12 min) but discovery never
# enumerates AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::Database at all - the log has no
# "Received N resources" line for the type, only for its parent
# AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::FlexibleServer, which is itself already excluded here
# for the same reason. Not the listParam bug: Database's List does carry a
# subscription-wide fallback that walks every flexible server. CRUD still runs:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=database
# database
# Slow chains, each with a timeout override below: the three AKS-backed
# fixtures stand up a cluster first (~5-10 min), virtual-machine-extension a
# VM, and the two Grafana fixtures a managed Grafana workspace (~5 min,
# billed hourly).
# flux-configuration excluded: Create alone runs past 20 min - an AKS
# cluster (~8 min) plus the flux extension install (~5 min) before the
# configuration itself is even attempted, and the cluster is billed the
# whole time. Nightly excludes it for the same reason. Run locally with a
# wide timeout:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=flux-configuration
# - flux-configuration
# maintenance-configuration excluded: the OOB-delete re-apply reaches a
# terminal Failed state after 14 min, and like flux-configuration it needs a
# billed AKS cluster stood up first. Nightly excludes it for the same reason.
# Run locally with a wide timeout:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=maintenance-configuration
# - maintenance-configuration
# trusted-access-role-binding excluded: Replace reaches a terminal Failed
# state after 13 min, and it needs the same billed AKS cluster as
# flux-configuration. Nightly excludes it for the same reason. Run locally:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=trusted-access-role-binding
# - trusted-access-role-binding
virtual-machine-extension
grafana
grafana-managed-private-endpoint
# Container Apps (Microsoft.App: managed-environment, container-app) excluded:
# a managed environment takes ~5 min to provision (container-app builds on top),
# exceeding the CI command timeout — same class as the AKS extension. Both are
# billed. CRUD validated via test-integration (mocked); run live locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=managed-environment TIMEOUT=15
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=container-app TIMEOUT=15
